newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen mostly down - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen mostly down - trade.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) report due on Friday will probably show a modest fall in copper stocks of 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes, Singapore-based metal dealers said.
"Copper should fall 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes," the general manager of a Japanese metal trading firm said. Several other dealers predicted a fall in the same range.
But one senior dealer at a European metal trading company said copper inventories could rise 6,000 tonnes or fall 3,000 tonnes when the LME report is issued at 0900 GMT.
"I don't think we'll see the big movement in copper we saw last Tuesday," one dealer said, refering to the 11,475 tonne rise in LME copper stocks in the last report on January 7.
Aluminium inventories in the LME will probably range between an increase of 1,000 tonnes and a fall of 2,000 tonnes, the traders said.
They said anywhere from 2,000 to 10,000 tonnes of copper would be arriving in Singapore warehouses soon. Most of it would probably come from China, dealers said.
"But I doubt if the material will get here quickly enough to be included in the LME report," one said.
The amount of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse soared to 39,750 tonnes on Tuesday, up 9,850 tonnes from the previous report on January 3.
Three month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at 0245 GMT at around US$2,268/73 a tonne against late trade in London on Thursday of $2,270/74 a tonne.
Aluminium was seen at around $1,606/11 a tonne at 0245 GMT compared with the late quote in London on Thursday of $1,605/08 a tonne, traders said.
